QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_72

question.text: Kalinga Venture Fund paid INR 5 crore carry to the GP after an early profitable exit. Two later deals fail, causing total fund profit to fall below GP's target share. Clawback kicks in for INR 2 crore. What mechanism ensures recovery?

answer.text: GP escrow account holding X% of interim carry + GP personal indemnity + Clawback provision in Contribution Agreement
LP bears the loss — clawback is only a moral clause

explanation.text: The Logic: Ch 9.3.2 emphasises clawback is only as good as GP balance sheet. Best practice: escrow holding a portion of interim carry, GP personal indemnity, and enforceable Clawback in the CA. The Trap: Option B is irrelevant. Option C doesn't exist. Option D defeats the purpose of clawback. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/C (Compliance) for enforcement; XIX-A/B for LP protection. Manager's Pro-Tip: Negotiate escrow at 30-50% of interim carry payments, released only on final fund reconciliation. Personal indemnity should survive GP change of control — important for multi-GP funds where an individual GP might exit.
